Faded points are cold charges (below {n} °C): shown for reference but left out of the figure — LFP reads low when cold. Charges ending near 100% count the most, where the BMS recalibrates the SoC.

Orange points are charges where the car was on and consuming power during the session — the energy/SoC ratio is distorted by onboard loads, so they're shown for reference but excluded from the health figure.

Orange points with a BMS recalibration label had a sudden SoC snap during charging — the BMS corrected its SoC estimate without matching energy, inflating the delta and deflating the capacity estimate. Shown for reference, excluded from the figure.
Violet points are charges that started below {n}% — near-empty, the BMS over-reports the SoC rise, so this reads as a capacity that's too low. Shown for reference, excluded from the figure.

Each point is the measured energy delivered during a charge (∫ voltage × current) divided by the SoC it added — an estimate of full-pack capacity. Only charges with a meaningful SoC rise and stored telemetry are used; single points are noisy, so the headline figure is averaged over the most recent charges. This is an estimate, not a lab measurement.

Each bar is a stretch the car sat parked and unplugged for at least an hour; the value is the SoC it lost, normalised to %/day. Stretches with any driving (speed or an odometer change) or charging are excluded, and tiny drops are treated as sensor noise. Pale bars are short or still-running parks, where a single 0.1% sensor step can inflate the daily rate — the ± in the tooltip shows by how much. The headline is total SoC lost ÷ total parked time across all parks, including those that lost nothing. Computed automatically from logged telemetry — no input needed.

Averaged over the kilometres of the trips that ran on the battery alone, and only where the car itself measured the energy. On a range-extender Mate blanks the figure for every trip the generator ran — a battery percentage stops measuring how efficiently the pack drove you once an engine is refilling it underneath. Those mixed trips still cover kilometres on battery and there is no way to tell which, so this is not every battery kilometre: it is the kilometres of the battery-only trips. Trips the cloud never reported are left out too, because for those the consumption is estimated from the battery percentage, not measured.

Per kWh BILLED: the wallbox counter on a home charge that has one, the charger's own kWh where you typed it, the battery energy everywhere else. The Overview shows a different figure, "Average price in battery", per kWh that actually REACHED the battery — higher, because the on-board charger turns 8–15% into heat before it gets there. Neither is wrong: you pay the first, a trip consumes the second.

kWh OUT of the charger: the wallbox counter where there is one, the charger's own kWh where you typed it, otherwise the battery figure — the only number that exists for a public charge nobody typed one for. Beside it, what actually reached the battery. The gap is what the on-board charger turned into heat: you pay the first, a trip consumes the second.

items.enValue: This is a beta-tester build whose purpose is to build REEV support for Mate. It captures all of your vehicle's raw signals locally and lets you export an encrypted bundle to send for analysis. Your data stays on your device until you choose to export it and attach it to an issue — GPS is removed and the bundle can only be opened by the maintainer. Statistics, Costs and Trips can be inaccurate in this build: no need to report a figure that just looks off. Do report anything that looks broken, though — an event counted more than once, a duplicate row, a value that cannot be true. By continuing you agree to take part in this data collection.
items.originalHr: Ovo je beta-tester verzija čija je svrha razvoj REEV podrške za Mate. Lokalno bilježi sve sirove signale vašeg vozila i omogućuje izvoz šifriranog paketa za analizu. Vaši podaci ostaju na vašem uređaju dok ih sami ne izvezete i priložite issueu — GPS je uklonjen, a paket može otvoriti samo održavatelj. Statistika, Troškovi i Vožnje mogu biti netočni u ovoj verziji: ne morate prijavljivati brojeve koji samo odstupaju. Svakako prijavite sve što izgleda pokvareno — događaj zbrojen više puta, duplicirani redak, nemoguću vrijednost. Nastavkom pristajete na sudjelovanje u ovom prikupljanju podataka.

items.enValue: Each point is the measured energy delivered during a charge (∫ voltage × current) divided by the SoC it added — an estimate of full-pack capacity. Only charges with a meaningful SoC rise and stored telemetry are used; single points are noisy, so the headline figure is averaged over the most recent charges. This is an estimate, not a lab measurement.

items.enValue: Each bar is a stretch the car sat parked and unplugged for at least an hour; the value is the SoC it lost, normalised to %/day. Stretches with any driving (speed or an odometer change) or charging are excluded, and tiny drops are treated as sensor noise. Pale bars are short or still-running parks, where a single 0.1% sensor step can inflate the daily rate — the ± in the tooltip shows by how much. The headline is total SoC lost ÷ total parked time across all parks, including those that lost nothing. Computed automatically from logged telemetry — no input needed.
items.originalHr: Svaki stupac je razdoblje u kojem je vozilo stajalo parkirano i odspojeno najmanje jedan sat; vrijednost je izgubljeni SoC normaliziran na %/dan. Razdoblja s bilo kakvom vožnjom (brzina ili promjena brojača kilometara) ili punjenjem su isključena, a sitni padovi smatraju se šumom senzora. Blijedi stupci su kratka ili još aktivna parkiranja gdje jedan korak senzora od 0,1% može napuhati dnevnu stopu — oznaka ± u opisu pokazuje za koliko. Glavna brojka je ukupno izgubljeni SoC ÷ ukupno vrijeme parkiranja za sva parkiranja, uključujući ona bez gubitka. Izračunato automatski iz zabilježene telemetrije — nije potreban unos.

items.enValue: Averaged over the kilometres of the trips that ran on the battery alone, and only where the car itself measured the energy. On a range-extender Mate blanks the figure for every trip the generator ran — a battery percentage stops measuring how efficiently the pack drove you once an engine is refilling it underneath. Those mixed trips still cover kilometres on battery and there is no way to tell which, so this is not every battery kilometre: it is the kilometres of the battery-only trips. Trips the cloud never reported are left out too, because for those the consumption is estimated from the battery percentage, not measured.
items.originalHr: Prosjek na kilometrima vožnji koje su se odvijale isključivo na bateriju, i to samo tamo gdje je samo vozilo izmjerilo energiju. Te mješovite vožnje i dalje prelaze kilometre na bateriju i ne može se razaznati koje, pa ovo nisu svi baterijski kilometri, već kilometri čisto baterijskih vožnji. Vožnje koje oblak nikad nije prijavio također su izostavljene jer se za njih potrošnja procjenjuje iz postotka baterije, a ne mjeri.

items.enValue: The weighted average price of the energy currently in the battery: every priced charge counts in proportion to the charge it added. It is the rate each trip's cost is worked out at — charging moves it, driving never does. On a charge billed on the kilowatt-hours the charger delivered — a wallbox meter, or the column's own figure typed in — it comes out above the tariff set in Charge Prices: the difference is what the on-board charger turned into heat before the energy reached the battery.
